title: Texas's 1st Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for Texas's 1st Congressional District pits incumbent Republican U.S. Representative Nathaniel Moran against Democratic nominee Yolanda Prince. The district covers much of East Texas, including Tyler, Longview, Nacogdoches, and Texarkana, and has been a Republican stronghold for decades—Donald Trump won the district with 74.3% in 2024. The race takes place amid mid-decade redistricting that was upheld by the U.S. Supreme Court in December 2025 after being challenged as a racial gerrymander. Moran, a conservative former Smith County judge, is heavily favored in the Solid R district, while Prince, a first-time candidate and personnel assistant, is campaigning on affordability, rural healthcare access, and Medicare for All.
polling_note: No district-specific opinion polls for Texas's 1st Congressional District were found. The only available polling is generic congressional ballot surveys for the entire state of Texas.

candidates.name: Nathaniel Moran
candidates.summary: Nathaniel Moran is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 1st Congressional District, first elected in 2022. A Republican, he previously served as Smith County Judge and on the Tyler City Council, and sits on the House Ways and Means Committee and the Select Committee on Strategic Competition with the Chinese Communist Party.

candidates.name: Yolanda Prince
candidates.summary: Yolanda Prince is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 1st Congressional District, having won the May 26, 2026 Democratic primary runoff with over 70% of the vote. She works as a Personnel Assistant at MD Anderson Cancer Center and is a first-time candidate for public office, running on a platform centered on affordability, rural healthcare access, Medicare for All, and raising the minimum wage.
